result.title: Scaling Graph Reasoning in Language Models with Learnable Graph Positional Encodings
result.summary: Solving reasoning tasks supported on graphs typically requires providing a Language Reasoning Model (LRM) with a serialized description of the graph. This approach results in the input length growing with the number of edges, which limits the size of the problems that can be solved. Furthermore, even when graphs fit in context, performance sharply decays as the graphs grow. We propose to address this by augmenting LRMs with scalable and permutation equivariant graph positional encodings that modulate attention logits. An additional post-fusion-style module incorporates structural information into hidden states. We compute these positional encodings using a GNN followed by a Graph Transformer. This eliminates the need for serialized adjacencies, reducing the context burden to $O(N)$. We jointly fine-tune the positional encoder and the LRM LoRA adapters using optimal solutions generated by graph-theoretic solvers, resulting in a computationally efficient method. Trained on small graphs, the model exhibits improved size-generalization across graph-theoretic tasks on graphs with up to 1,000 nodes, and produces fewer tokens than a conventional LRM. Additionally, we observe that our model remains robust to node relabelings. Evaluations on graph-theoretic benchmarks also show that performance on small graphs is preserved.

AI.brief_summary: 该文让语言推理模型不做图邻接的序列化输入，而用 GNN 与 Graph Transformer 学习置换等变的图位置编码，调制注意力 logits 并经后融合模块写入隐状态，再用图求解器生成的最优解联合微调编码器与 LoRA，从而在至多 1000 节点的图上改善规模泛化。
AI.relevance_reason: 其以「注意力偏置＋隐状态融合」注入非文本结构信息并考察规模泛化，可能为 LVR 中视觉结构证据如何进入内部状态及长度泛化提供方法线索，但无直接视觉或多模态推理验证，需核查其状态是否真正被后续推理使用。
